Risk calculators have limitations in predicting surgical site infections (SSIs). While they can identify patients at higher risk for SSI, their accuracy is limited compared to other predictive models. Current models have shown modest success in identifying patients at risk for SSI.

To accurately predict surgical site occurrences, a more comprehensive approach that considers multiple factors, including patient demographics, comorbidities, and surgical specifics, is needed. Risk calculators should be used as one tool among many when assessing the risk of SSI.
